variables.ticket.description:
# eh run: add `--timeout <seconds>` so hung lanes fail loudly

## Problem

`eh run` has no deadline on the spawned harness. A lane that hangs (harness bug, dead provider connection, stuck tool call) blocks forever, and every orchestrator must implement its own external watchdog-and-kill. Multi-lane review orchestration currently documents "kill it by hand after ~15 minutes" as the workaround.

## Context

* Branch from `origin/main` (local main is 7 commits behind).
* SIGINT/SIGTERM *forwarding* to the child already exists in `src/headless-run.ts` (handler installed/removed around the child lifecycle) and is exercised by the test named "forwards termination signals and removes the Grok prompt file" in `src/headless-run.test.ts` — locate by test name, not line number. The timeout hooks into this exact plumbing point.
* A SIGTERM'd child already yields exit code `128 + signal` via the existing derivation (`completed.code ?? (signalNumber ? 128 + signalNumber : 1)`), so a timed-out run is distinguishable today without new exit-code machinery. The reserved-exit-codes ticket owns any future remapping; do not add one here. Note the accepted limitation: by exit code alone, a timeout is indistinguishable from any other SIGTERM (both `143`) — orchestrators that need certainty read the `run.error` event.
* The `--cwd` and exit-codes tickets touch the same region of `headless-run.ts`. Land serially — suggested order: cwd, then this ticket, then exit codes.
* No new runtime deps (repo rule) — `setTimeout`/`AbortController` only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `eh run` accepts `--timeout <seconds>`. On expiry: eh emits a `run.error` event naming the timeout and the configured limit, then sends SIGTERM; `run.completed` is still the final event. Proof: subprocess test with a fake harness that sleeps past the deadline, asserting the event sequence and child termination.
- [ ] If the child ignores SIGTERM, eh escalates to SIGKILL after a grace period of 10 seconds, defined as a named constant and injectable (option or env var) so the escalation test doesn't sleep 10 real seconds. Proof: subprocess test with a fake harness that traps SIGTERM, asserting SIGKILL termination and the same event-ordering guarantee.
- [ ] A non-positive, non-integer, or non-numeric `--timeout` value fails preflight before spawn with a clear error and nonzero exit. Proof: subprocess tests for `0`, a negative value, and a non-numeric value, asserting the fake harness was never invoked.
- [ ] Invariant: the timeout never affects a run that completes in time — a child that closes before the deadline produces the same events and exit code as a run without the flag, and the timer is cleaned up (no hanging process, no stray kill of a reused pid). Proof: subprocess test running a fast fake harness with a generous `--timeout`, asserting the event stream matches the no-flag run and the eh process exits promptly.
- [ ] Omitting the flag preserves today's behavior (no deadline).

## Out of Scope

* Token/cost budgets (a different resource limit).
* A config-level default timeout; per-invocation flag only.
* Reserved exit-code assignment for timeouts (see the exit-codes ticket).

## Verification

* `pnpm lint:ci`; `bun test src/headless-run.test.ts`; full `pnpm test`.
* Version bump required; update README `### Headless runs`, DESIGN.md `Headless execution`, `docs/qa/eh-cli.md`.

## Delegability

```yaml
design_freedom: low
verification_strength: high
silent_failure_cost: medium
context_volatility: low
recommended_tier: medium
recommended_effort: medium
```
